literal: Painful is living in a town without companions; even more painful than that is separation from beloved ones.
translation: Living in a town where one has no companions is painful; but far more painful than that is separation from those who are beloved.
modern: உறவினர்கள் இல்லாத ஊரில் வாழ்வது துன்பமானது; அதைவிடத் துன்பமானது அன்பானவரைப் பிரிந்து வாழ்வது ஆகும்.
explanation: The couplet compares two painful situations to highlight the extreme distress of separation. Living in a town without friends or relatives (இனன் இல் ஊர்) is hard and lonely. However, the poet states that separation from one's beloved (இனியார் பிரிவு) is even more painful (அதனினும் இன்னாது) than such a friendless existence. The words 'இன்னாது' (painful) and 'இனியார்' (sweet/beloved ones) beautifully contrast the bitterness of loneliness with the sweetness of love.
